text:
maria_cs: FYI Helix Labs just opened a support ticket — they’re seeing 95th/99th tail spikes on text-generation API since 03:30 UTC, p95 ~800ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~3s -> 6s. Happened after the midnight rolling deploy. They say it’s affecting inference latency for their chat product. @jordan_sre any quick thoughts? :eyes:

jordan_sre: Thanks Maria. Can you paste the customer request IDs (or a few examples)? Also which model/table they’re hitting and the route?

maria_cs: Route: /v1/generate, model: redwood-7b-instruct, example req id: hx-req-20260315-01, hx-req-02. Customer says latency is mostly at tail for tenant helix-labs and they’ve seen errors like 429 and occasional 504s.

jordan_sre: 429s + p99 spikes -> suspicious of per-tenant throttles or a noisy neighbor causing queueing. Sam, can you pull per-tenant QPS and queue length for helix-labs around 03:00-04:00 UTC?

sam_support: On it. Querying metrics now. Here’s a quick PromQL I ran: ```sum(rate(requests_total{tenant="helix-labs",route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (instance)``` Results: a single instance at ~220 rps for that tenant while others are ~10-30 rps. Queue depth spiked to ~120 at 03:14 UTC.

jordan_sre: That’s a pretty clear noisy-tenant pattern. Can you also pull per-instance latency distribution? ```histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant="helix-labs"}[5m])) by (le,instance))```

prometheus-bot: Query executed in 120ms. p99 per-instance: instance-a: 5.2s, instance-b: 0.4s, instance-c: 0.35s.

jordan_sre: So traffic concentrated on instance-a -> its p99 far higher. Need to check whether instance-a had CPU/gpu contention or a model caching issue. @lee_platform can you check instance-a resource metrics (GPU utilization, mem, kernel busy) and whether any other tenant injected heavy KV-cache warmups?

lee_platform: Looking at instance-a: GPU utilization peaked at 98% between 03:10-03:20, persistent context switching seen on host (nvidia-smi shows multiple processes). There’s also a large embed job from tenant "datasnap" that started at 03:05 -> likely noisy neighbor. I see no infra OOMs.

jordan_sre: That matches noisy neighbor. Two immediate mitigations: 1) Move helix-labs to a different instance (scale up and route them away from instance-a). 2) Apply a temporary per-tenant throttle/allowlist override so helix-labs gets higher priority. We can also escalate to dedicated pool if they want.

maria_cs: Customer asked for hotfix asap; they can’t tolerate p99 > 500ms for their SLA. They’re open to a short-term dedicated reservation if needed.

lee_platform: I can issue a routing change to rebalance tenants off instance-a. Applying a per-tenant routing policy: ```yaml
route_overrides:
  tenant: helix-labs
  prefer_pool: general-02
  priority: high
``` Pushing in 2m.

deploy-bot: Rollout started by lee_platform at 2026-03-15T03:45:12Z -> route override apply to pool general-02 (canary 10%).

jordan_sre: While that rolls, Sam please create a temporary throttle policy to protect the instance and give helix-labs an allowlist bypass for burst. Config: ```json
{"tenant":"helix-labs","throttle_override":{"max_qps":400,"burst":200,"priority":"high"}}```
Also add a canary check every 30s to measure p95/p99.

sam_support: Created and applied throttle override at 03:47 UTC. Canaries start now, pinging results.

prometheus-bot: Canary metrics (03:48): helix-labs p95=220ms, p99=360ms. Instance-a p99 dropping to 1.2s. Request rate for helix-labs now distributed across instance-a/b/c.

jordan_sre: Good — looks like routing + throttle helped. Next steps: 1) Keep throttle override for 30m and monitor. 2) Notify infra to throttle heavy embed jobs from datasnap or move them to a separate dedicated pool. 3) Offer Helix a short-term dedicated capacity (2x small gpus) while they evaluate long-term options.

lee_platform: Noted. I’ve put an auto-quota rule to limit large embed jobs that start without approval. Temporarily suspended the datasnap job pending approval.

maria_cs: Customer updated ticket — after 10 minutes they report UX improvement and fewer errors. They asked for a summary of what we changed.

jordan_sre: Draft summary to send to customer: "We detected a noisy tenant (datasnap) causing GPU contention on instance-a which produced long queues for helix-labs. We rebalanced helix-labs traffic away from the hotspot and applied a temporary throttle override/allowlist to prioritize their requests. Observed p99 drop from ~6s to ~360ms. We’ve suspended the offending job and proposed a short-term dedicated pool to Helix while they decide on long-term options."

maria_cs: Customer replied: "Thanks — please provision dedicated pool while we confirm expected load. Will accept engagement for 2-week dedicated eval." :thumbsup:

jordan_sre: I’ll follow up with infra to provision a 2x-small dedicated pool and schedule a cleanup to make sure datasnap jobs are gated. Also file a follow-up to build an automated detector for tenant-localized p99 spikes that suggests routing changes. Ticket -> CS-4821.

sam_support: Logging actions for audits: ```diff
- tenant: datasnap
+ job: embed-run-20260315
  action: suspended
  timestamp: 2026-03-15T03:55:00Z
```

lee_platform: Post-mortem notes: root cause noisy neighbor embed + insufficient tenancy isolation on shared GPU pool. Mitigations applied: routing rebalance, throttle override, embed job gating, offer dedicated capacity. Long term: quota-based scheduling and automatic per-tenant router reshuffle when queue depth > threshold.

maria_cs: Closing loop with customer and scheduling follow-up call tomorrow. Thanks team! :heart:

-- end of thread
